pattern.description: Monospace uppercase line 'AVAILABLE NOW' is typed one character per step behind a solid white block cursor on a near-black starfield; the line stays horizontally centred, so each keystroke nudges the already-typed text left while the cursor advances right.
pattern.why_premium: Strictly rhythmic step timing (energy spikes at a fixed ~5-frame interval) with no easing reads as a precise terminal/command-line voice that matches a developer tool; the restrained palette (white mono type, single block cursor, black field) keeps all attention on the CTA phrase.

build_hint.gsap: Split the line into chars (SplitText type:'chars'), set all autoAlpha:0, then tl.to(chars, {autoAlpha:1, duration:0, stagger:{each:0.083, ease:'none'}}) ; keep the text container centred (text-align:center) so it re-centres per char, and move the block cursor with each char via an onUpdate/stagger callback (gsap.set cursor x to the last visible char's right edge); no tween easing — ease:'steps(1)'. Cursor stays visible (optional blink after settle with repeat:-1, ease:'steps(1)').
build_hint.remotion: const n = Math.floor(frame / 5) (~83 ms per char at 60 fps); render text.slice(0, n) in a centred monospace flex row followed by the block cursor element so layout moves the cursor; no spring or interpolate easing (hard step per char); optional cursor blink via Math.floor(frame/30)%2 after the last char.

notes: Event window starts mid-typing ('AVAIL' already present at f1479); earlier chars belong outside this event. Energy shows 8 discrete spikes every 5 frames (B, L, E, space, N, O, W). Facts camera reports move 'none' but scale 1.19 / pan_x -0.07 — likely an artefact of the centred line re-flowing left, not a real camera move; worth a human check. Per-word split b03/b04 chosen over union b01 so cursor b05 is separate.
